pronunciation.notes: Stress fal. The a is short.

word.shortDefinition: Used to say you like something: Das gefällt mir.

intro.title: The Like button
paragraphs: If you've used Facebook in German, you've clicked gefallen many times. The Like button says Gefällt mir: it pleases me.
That's the whole secret of this verb. In English you like the thing. In German the thing pleases you. The sentence is built the other way round.

etymology.title: Where it comes from
etymology.summary: Something that gefällt you is something that has fallen out the right way for you, like a lucky throw of the dice.

bonus.note: Same spelling, but a noun: Kannst du mir einen Gefallen tun? Can you do me a favour?

tables.title: Who's who
tables.intro: The thing you like is the subject, so the verb agrees with it. The person who likes it goes in the dative.
notes: Das Kleid gefällt mir. Die Schuhe gefallen mir. The verb changes with the thing, not with you.
Past: Der Film hat mir gefallen.

keyTrap.title: The big trap: making yourself the subject
keyTrap.explanation: English speakers put themselves first, as the one doing the liking. With gefallen, you're the one being pleased, so you go in the dative.

correct.note: Same meaning, with the emphasis on you.
Or use mögen, which works like English.

commonMistakes.title: Food uses schmecken
commonMistakes.explanation: Gefallen is for how something looks, sounds or feels. For taste, Germans say schmecken.

commonMistakes.title: Plural things
commonMistakes.explanation: When the thing is plural, the verb is too.

commonMistakes.title: First impressions
commonMistakes.explanation: Gefallen is about first impressions. For a friend you know well, mögen sounds warmer.

examples.english: I like Berlin (what I've seen of it).

sampleSentences.german: Wie gefällt dir die neue Wohnung?
sampleSentences.english: How do you like the new flat?

sampleSentences.german: Die Kinder gefallen der Oma sehr.
Kannst du mir einen Gefallen tun?
sampleSentences.english: Can you do me a favour?

quiz.explanation: The person who likes it is in the dative: mir.
Schuhe is plural, so the verb is plural.

quiz.prompt: Der Kuchen ___ mir sehr gut. (it tastes good)
quiz.fullAnswer: Der Kuchen schmeckt mir sehr gut.

quiz.explanation: Berlin is one thing, so the verb is singular.

quiz.prompt: Wie hat ___ der Film gefallen? (you, informal)
quiz.explanation: The person who likes it is in the dative: dir.

memoryHook: Think of the Like button: Gefällt mir. The thing pleases me, so the thing comes first and I'm the mir.
